Rules of Mahjong

I’m not explaining every rule, just ones needed to understand this document. I also strongly suggest just watching one game of physical mahjong even if you don’t understand anything so you can grasp how tiles are placed and how turns and discarded tiles are treated since Akagi’s cheats often involve messing with the way tiles are physically placed.
Riichi mahjong is the mahjong played in Akagi, and in Riichi mahjong there are four players in a square table with each player sitting on each side.

Mahjong involves taking turns pulling and discarding tiles from the stack of tiles to slowly form your hand. You start with 13 tiles in front of you initially and pull and discard tiles to slowly form a hand.

Every round there is a Oya or house that is basically the player that turns start on and if they win they get extra scores compared to other players but lose more scores if they lose. The house rotates for every round but if the house wins they remain as the house to the next turn.

All tile types include Mazu, Pinzu, Souzu tiles which are 3 different types of numbered tiles and are like the colors in a set of trump card. So there is 1-9 manzu tiles, 1-9 souzu tiles and 1-9 pinzu tiles. There are also word tiles (Ton (written with the West Kanji), Nan (Written with the South Kanji), Xia (Written with the East Kanji), Pei (Written with the North Kanji)) as well as 3 other types of words not related to directions which are Haku, Hatsu, Chun. There are 4 of each type of tile, so there are 4 of 3man tiles and 4 of Haku tiles for example.

A winning hand can be made with 14 tiles so in your usual state you would have 13 tiles and once you reach Tenpai (one step away from victory) the one tile you need will be your 14th tile to form a win. To actually make your hand a valid one to win and to actually earn you any scores it needs to have a Yaku. Most Yaku are formed in the general hand shape which is “one pair of the same tile called the head” and “three triplets, the triplets can either be numbered tiles that are in numerical order or same tiles that are identical”. There are hands that can be formed that does not follow the general hand shape but it's rare, the ones that sometimes appear are 7 pairs, (your hand is composed on 7 pairs) or a Kokushi-Musou which is just having all types of 1,9 and word tiles and making one pair using it.
Yaku are general patterns in your hand that assign a hand a certain score value.

Winning by pulling the tile you need on your own is called a Tsumo and in this case the 3 other players need to pay for your hands total cost and if the player who won is not the house the house has to pay extra. If it was a Ron meaning your final winning tile was taken from a player who discarded it, the player who discarded it is burdened to pay all the points.

Dora is one of the key factors important in a lot of decision making regarding mahjong. When forming a hand you generally want as many Yaku as possible as a lot of Yaku can co-exist in a single hand. For example a Tanyao is a Yaku given to a hand that does not have any word tiles or 1 or 9 tiles. A Chin-Itsu is a Yaku that is given to a hand that is entirely composed of one suit of number tiles, meaning it only uses either Manzu, Pinzu or Souzu tiles and no word tiles. So a hand like
(2man, 3man, 4man, 5man, 6man, 7man, 6man, 7man, 8man, 2man, 2man, 2man, 3man, 3man)

The following hand forms a standard hand shape and is composed entirely of Mazu tiles and has no 1,9 tiles and no word tiles so it's a Tanyao. It also is entirely composed of Mazu tiles so it also has a Chin-Itsu. Like this a lot of players move to form as much Yaku as possible but there is a rule that makes this a lot easier which is the Dora. A Dora is a certain tile that changes every round and just by having it, it adds one “han” to your hand. A han is the number that increases as you form more Yaku and each Yaku is given a han number meaning how much han is given to a hand for that certain Yaku and once someone wins with their hand the number of han directly influences the score they earn. By having a Dora it automatically adds 1 han per one Dora a person has. The Dora is decided by a special section of the stack which is usually not drawn from, a designated place of the stack is flipped to reveal a certain tile and the next number of the tile will become the Dora so if its a 1man then the Dora is a 2man. If it's 9sou the Dora will be a 1sou. If it's a word tile, the direction tile goes as Pei => Ton => Nan => Xia => Pei, so if it's a Ton the Dora will be a Nan and so on. For Haku Hatsu Chun the order is Chun => Haku => Hatsu => Chun. Keep in mind a Dora goes not count as a Yaku so the rule where “a hand can not win unless it has at least one Yaku” can not be overcome by having a Dora in your hand, the Dora only affects the hand when it's time to calculate the score of the hand after winning.

Taking the other players' discarded tiles is what makes mahjong so complex. As others discard their tiles you can take them and other players can do the same. A Ron can be done when you have a Tenpai (one step away from a winning hand) and someone discards the tile you need, it doesn’t matter who discarded it or who’s turn it is, you immediately say Ron and open your hand and you win the round. The other way you can take the others tiles even when you aren’t Tenpai is with a Pon or Chi. Similarly you say out loud if it's a Chi or Pon. If you have a pair of the same tile and you find the third one discarded by another player you can call Pon and take it but the two pair you already had and the tile you took are displayed to all players and moved to the edge of the table, its still a part of your hand but its fixed and you can’t change or discard the triplet formed. A Chi is similar to a Pon since it fixes the triplet and you can do it even if your not Tenpai but Chi is a triplet where its in numerical order not a triplet of the same tile, if you have 2 tiles of numerical order and you find the player to your left discard a tile to complete your triplet you can call Chi, you can only call from the player on your left. Pon and Chi are only applicable for triplets not pairs.

Another call you can do is a Kan. If you have 4 of the same tile you can say Kan in your turn and show it to everyone, then the 4 tile set is considered one triplet, and because then your winning hand will be composed of 15 tiles not 14 since one of your triplets is formed with 1 extra tile, you need to substitute the extra tile by pulling another tile from a special stack specifically for pulling when a player does a Kan. Also by doing a Kan a extra Dora indicator tile is added.

Because of Ron players need to be aware of other players' discarded tiles to estimate their hand and make sure to avoid it. Pon and Chi are called “calling” and it allows you to form hands faster but it limits the part of the hand you can actually discard so it limits your discardable tiles which can be dangerous since if you don’t have enough tiles you might not have safe tiles. Also certain Yaku are turned invalid if you do a Pon or Chi.
The Yaku that appear in this game and is significant is the following :
Riichi

- once you reach Tenpai without calling Pon or Chi you can say Riichi which tells everyone that you are Tenpai and put your 1000 point stick in the table as wager, if you win that round the 1000 point is given back to you but if someone else does, your 1000 point gets taken away. It's a 1 Han Yaku.
Hon-Itsu
- Forming your hand by only using one suit of number tiles and word tiles, you can call but it reduces the number of Hans the Yaku grants from 3 to 2.
Chin-Itsu
- Hon-Itsu but without using word tiles. If you call the number of Han this Yaku grants drops from 6 to 5.
Yaku-Hai
- By having a triplet of either a Haku, Hatsu or Chun it is automatically a Yaku and gives 1han, you can call Pon or Chi as well.
Chanta

- Hand composed in the regular 1pair 4 triplet form but all pair and triplets contain at least 1 of the following types of tiles : (word tile, 1 tile of any suit, 9 tile of any suit). Calling drops the Han this Yaku grants from 2 to 1.
3 Kantsu
- Made when you do 3 Kan’s. grants 2 han and you are allowed to Call as much as you want.
3 Ankou
- Made when you form 3 Ankou which are triplets that are composed of all the same tiles and made without calling, the fourth triplet can be made by calling.
Rinshan Kaihou
- Once you do a Kan you pull from a special stack, if you get a Tsumo from the pull you do from the special stack this Yaku is given.
